title: DFS: pre / in / post

why_it_exists.problem: When traversing a tree, you must visit every node, but different problems require you to access a node's data at different stages of the recursion. A single traversal order cannot solve all problems.
why_it_exists.better_idea: Depth-First Search (DFS) provides three distinct visit orders—Pre-order, In-order, and Post-order—which differ ONLY by WHEN you record or process the current node relative to making the left and right recursive calls.

mental_model.intuition: Three lines of code: recurse left, recurse right, and 'visit'. The order you write them dictates the traversal.
mental_model.description: Pre-order processes the parent before its children (top-down). In-order processes the left child, then the parent, then the right child. Post-order processes both children completely before processing the parent (bottom-up).
mental_model.repeated_decision: Do I record this node BEFORE, BETWEEN, or AFTER its two recursive calls?

explanation:
Depth-First Search (DFS) variants are just the same three operations rearranged. 

**Pre-order (Node, Left, Right):** You visit the node immediately upon reaching it, before delegating to the children. This top-down sequence is perfect for duplicating or serializing a tree, as it records the root first to provide an unambiguous starting point for deserialization.

**In-order (Left, Node, Right):** You fully process the left subtree, then the current node, then the right subtree. The headline use for this is Binary Search Trees (BSTs). Because a BST places smaller elements to the left and larger elements to the right, an in-order traversal of a BST naturally yields the nodes in perfectly ascending sorted order.

**Post-order (Left, Right, Node):** You delay processing the current node until both of its children have completely finished and returned their results. This bottom-up data flow is mandatory when a parent depends on the results of its descendants. For example, to calculate a tree's height or to safely delete a tree from memory, you must process the children first.

key_points.title: Which order for which job
key_points.detail: Pre-order for top-down cloning/serialization. In-order for sorted iteration of a BST. Post-order for bottom-up tasks like calculating height or freeing memory.

common_mistakes.title: Thinking in-order sorts any tree
common_mistakes.explanation: In-order traversal only produces a sorted sequence if the tree is a Binary Search Tree (BST). It does not magically sort a generic binary tree.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming the orders visit different nodes
common_mistakes.explanation: All three DFS traversals visit the exact same nodes, exactly the same number of times. The only difference is the sequence in which the node's payload is recorded.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting the null base case
common_mistakes.explanation: Always start your recursive traversal by checking `if node is None: return`. Failing to do so causes crashes on leaf children.

recall_questions.q: What is the exact sequence of steps for a Post-order traversal?
recall_questions.answer: Recurse Left, Recurse Right, Visit Node.

recall_questions.q: Which DFS traversal is used to get a sorted output from a Binary Search Tree?
Why is Post-order traversal required for safely deleting a tree?
recall_questions.answer: Because a parent node cannot be deleted until its children have been safely removed; otherwise, the pointers to the children are lost, causing memory leaks.

oa_questions.question: Given the root of a binary tree, return the postorder traversal of its nodes' values.
oa_questions.answer: Write a recursive function that calls itself on `node.left`, then `node.right`, and finally appends `node.val` to a result array.
oa_questions.approach: This tests the exact definition of post-order: Left, Right, Node.

oa_questions.question: Find the Kth smallest element in a Binary Search Tree.
oa_questions.answer: Perform an in-order traversal and return the Kth node you visit. Because in-order traverses a BST in ascending order, the Kth visited node is the Kth smallest.
oa_questions.approach: Connect the in-order invariant to the BST sorting property.

engineering_examples.title: Tree Serialization
engineering_examples.problem: Saving a tree structure to disk or a string so it can be perfectly reconstructed later.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Pre-order traversal records the parent before the children, so the deserializer knows exactly which node is the root of the current subtree when reading it back.

engineering_examples.title: Abstract Syntax Tree Evaluation
engineering_examples.problem: Evaluating a mathematical expression tree like `(2+3)*4`.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Post-order traversal is used by compilers to ensure leaf operands are evaluated before applying the parent operator node.
